# `Q-12-10` — Listing Markdown Re-parse Diagnostics

> Re-parsing the markdown produced by the listing template
> surfaced one or more diagnostics.

## What this means

A listing renders in two steps. First, Quarto runs the listing
template (a built-in or a custom doctemplate) over the listing's
items and produces a string of markdown. Then it parses that
markdown back into an AST so the result can be spliced into the
host document.

If the second parse surfaces diagnostics, this warning fires.
The message includes how many diagnostics the re-parse produced
and the title of the first one, so you can find the underlying
issue.

## Why this happens

Two known triggers:

- **Item metadata contains markdown that does not survive
  template interpolation.** A title with raw `[` characters, an
  unbalanced `*`, or similar — the template emitted the
  character literally and the re-parse complained.
- **A custom template produced syntactically invalid output.**
  An accidental unterminated fence or unescaped delimiter that
  the template author did not anticipate.

## How to fix

Inspect the first diagnostic the warning mentions — its error
code (`Q-2-*`) and message point at what the re-parser found
broken. Then trace it back to either the offending item
metadata or the custom template.
